hints: Think about what type of bond breaking must start reaction 1 and what energy source can split $\text{Cl}_{2}$ into radicals.
walkthrough:
Link the mechanism to the energy needed**
Reaction 1 converts cyclohexane to chlorocyclohexane by free radical substitution. The very first event must be splitting $\text{Cl}_{2}$ into two $\text{Cl}\cdot$ radicals by homolytic fission. That $\text{Cl-Cl}$ bond will not break on its own at room temperature, it needs energy from light.

hints: Recall the three stages of free radical substitution and match $\text{Cl}_{2} \rightarrow 2\text{Cl}\cdot$ to formation of radicals from a molecule.
Look at the first propagation step where $\text{Cl}\cdot$ removes H from cyclohexane, what small H containing molecule must form alongside the carbon radical?
Decide why the step that makes chlorocyclohexane from the cyclohexyl radical plus $\text{Cl}_{2}$ is still propagation rather than termination.
For the final termination step, join the two radicals shown to give the single stable organic product with no new radical.
walkthrough:
Name the radical forming step**
$\text{Cl}_{2} \rightarrow 2\text{Cl}\cdot$ creates radicals from a stable molecule with nothing consumed except $\text{Cl}_{2}$. That is the definition of initiation. It starts the chain.

Complete the first propagation equation**
In $\text{C}_{6}\text{H}_{12} + \text{Cl}\cdot \rightarrow \text{C}_{6}\text{H}_{11}\cdot +$ ?, a $\text{Cl}\cdot$ radical abstracts H from cyclohexane. The H joins Cl to make $\text{HCl}$, leaving the cyclohexyl radical $\text{C}_{6}\text{H}_{11}\cdot$. One radical is used and a new carbon radical is made, so the chain continues.

Name the second radical to molecule step**
$\text{C}_{6}\text{H}_{11}\cdot + \text{Cl}_{2} \rightarrow \text{C}_{6}\text{H}_{11}\text{Cl} + \text{Cl}\cdot$ uses a radical and regenerates a new $\text{Cl}\cdot$. Because a radical product is reformed to keep the cycle going, this is still propagation, the second propagation step.

Complete the termination step**
$\text{C}_{6}\text{H}_{11}\cdot + \text{Cl}\cdot \rightarrow$ ? joins two radicals with no radical left over. That is termination. Pairing the dots gives the stable product chlorocyclohexane, $\text{C}_{6}\text{H}_{11}\text{Cl}$.

Final answer: Row 1 name: initiation
Row 2 missing product: $\text{HCl}$
Row 3 name: propagation
Row 4 product: chlorocyclohexane, $\text{C}_{6}\text{H}_{11}\text{Cl}$ (cyclohexane ring with Cl substituent).

hints: Compare the structures in reaction 2, chlorocyclohexane loses Cl plus H from an adjacent carbon to form $\text{C=C}$, what class of reaction removes a small molecule to create a double bond?
walkthrough:
Spot what is lost to make the double bond**
Look closely at the change: chlorocyclohexane has only single bonds, cyclohexene has one $\text{C=C}$. To do that, $\text{HCl}$ is removed from the molecule. Removing a small molecule to form a double bond is elimination, here specifically dehydrohalogenation.

hints: Recognise that converting cyclohexene to $\text{HO}_{2}\text{C}(\text{CH}_{2})_{4}\text{CO}_{2}\text{H}$ breaks the $\text{C=C}$ completely to give two $\text{-CO}_{2}\text{H}$ groups, which needs strong oxidation.
Recall which oxidising agent for alkenes must be hot, concentrated and acidified to give cleavage to acids rather than the cold dilute diol route.
walkthrough:
Identify the oxidation level change**
Cyclohexene is a ring with one $\text{C=C}$. Adipic acid is an open chain dicarboxylic acid, $\text{HO}_{2}\text{C}(\text{CH}_{2})_{4}\text{CO}_{2}\text{H}$. The double bond carbon atoms have been fully oxidised to carboxylic acid groups and the ring has been cleaved. That needs vigorous oxidative cleavage, not mild oxidation.

Select the exact reagent and conditions**
The AS reagent for this is potassium manganate(VII), $\text{KMnO}_{4}$, acidified with dilute sulfuric acid. It must be hot and concentrated to force cleavage to the diacid. Cold dilute $\text{KMnO}_{4}$ would stop at the diol, so state hot and concentrated clearly.

hints: List the functional groups unique to cyclohexene ($\text{C=C}$, alkene $\text{C-H}$) versus those unique to adipic acid ($\text{O-H}$ in acid, $\text{C=O}$, $\text{C-O}$).
Recall which IR peaks prove an alkene, the $\text{C=C}$ stretch and the alkene $\text{=C-H}$ stretch above $3000 \text{ cm}^{-1}$.
Recall which IR peaks prove a carboxylic acid, the very broad $\text{O-H}$ absorption, the strong $\text{C=O}$ absorption and the $\text{C-O}$ absorption.
walkthrough:
Use alkene absorptions to spot cyclohexene**
Cyclohexene contains $\text{C=C}$ which gives a peak at 1500-1680 $\text{cm}^{-1}$. Adipic acid has no $\text{C=C}$, so this peak is absent in its spectrum. Cyclohexene also has alkene $\text{=C-H}$ bonds giving a $\text{C-H}$ stretch at 3000-3100 $\text{cm}^{-1}$, just above $3000 \text{ cm}^{-1}$, while adipic acid has only alkane $\text{C-H}$ and acid $\text{O-H}$ in that region.

Use the acid O-H absorption to spot adipic acid**
Adipic acid has two $\text{-CO}_{2}\text{H}$ groups. The $\text{O-H}$ in a carboxylic acid gives a very broad, strong absorption at 2500-3000 $\text{cm}^{-1}$ which dominates the spectrum. Cyclohexene has no $\text{O-H}$, so this broad band is missing.

Use C=O and C-O to confirm the acid**
Adipic acid shows a strong sharp $\text{C=O}$ stretch at 1640-1750 $\text{cm}^{-1}$ and a $\text{C-O}$ stretch at 1040-1300 $\text{cm}^{-1}$. Cyclohexene contains neither $\text{C=O}$ nor $\text{C-O}$, so both are absent. Any three of these paired comparisons with correct bond and wavenumber range earns full credit.

Final answer: Any three of:
Cyclohexene shows $\text{C=C}$ stretch at 1500-1680 $\text{cm}^{-1}$, adipic acid does not.
Cyclohexene shows $\text{=C-H}$ (alkene $\text{C-H}$) stretch at 3000-3100 $\text{cm}^{-1}$, adipic acid does not.
Adipic acid shows $\text{O-H}$ (in $\text{CO}_{2}\text{H}$) broad absorption at 2500-3000 $\text{cm}^{-1}$, cyclohexene does not.
Adipic acid shows $\text{C=O}$ stretch at 1640-1750 $\text{cm}^{-1}$, cyclohexene does not.
Adipic acid shows $\text{C-O}$ stretch at 1040-1300 $\text{cm}^{-1}$, cyclohexene does not.
